\[
G_x = I(x + 1, y) - I(x - 1, y),
\qquad
\theta = \arctan \frac{G_y}{G_x} \bmod 180^\circ,
\qquad
h_c(b) = \sum_{x \in c,\ \theta(x) \in b} \lvert G(x) \rvert
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(G_x, G_y\): The centered differences
- \(\theta\): The unsigned gradient direction
- \(h_c(b)\): The weight of bin b in cell c

The gradient comes from centered differences, with its magnitude and an unsigned direction from 0 to 180 degrees. Each cell gets a histogram of the directions of its pixels, weighted by the magnitude. Dalal and Triggs then normalize blocks of cells together, so the descriptor does not depend on the lighting, and chain all blocks into one long vector for a classifier. The view of scikit-image draws each cell histogram as lines through the cell center, one per bin, as bright as its weight. Each line lies across its gradient direction, so it runs along the edges in the cell. The view shows the cell histograms before the block normalization, so the block settings only change the descriptor.
